subject: Operational assurance & SLA upgrade pathway for renewal and capacity expansion
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya@linestream.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@linestream.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: SLA + capacity questions for upcoming term

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you're well — our renewal for Linestream is coming up in January and the product team has asked us to firm up support and latency commitments before we sign. High-level asks from our side:

- Move to a Premium SLA with a 99.9% availability guarantee (currently on Standard).
- Target p95 latency <= 300ms for text generation requests for the core chat route.
- Reserve additional capacity: +4 dedicated GPU slots with burst available for seasonal spikes.
- Clear runbook for degradations and 24/7 oncall escalation cadence.

Can you share what that would look like as a renewal amendment (term changes / pricing impact)? If useful, I'll include procurement and legal to speed approvals. Attaching last quarter's usage report for context.

Thanks,
Anya
Senior PM, Linestream

Attachment: usage_report_q4.csv (summary CSV)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya@linestream.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@linestream.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Nov 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: SLA + capacity questions for upcoming term

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage file. We're excited to keep Linestream on the platform and support your scale.

Quick summary of what I can propose now (we'll formalize in an SLA annex + pricing addendum):

- Premium SLA: 99.9% uptime, with financial credits for sustained breaches.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 300ms for your primary chat/model route in us-west region; targeted p99 mitigation plan and periodic performance reports.
- Capacity: reserve +4 GPUs for dedicated capacity with a 20% burst pool (elastic short-term capacity) for seasonality.
- Support: 24/7 priority queue, named oncall with 30-minute response for Sev1, quarterly operational review (QBR) + playbook handoff.

Estimated commercial impact: uplift of ~22% on current committed spend (ballpark) — I can get exact numbers once Karthik runs pricing for dedicated reservation + credits.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I will loop in Karthik (pricing) and Priyom (capacity/ops) to validate technical feasibility and firm up numbers.
2) If that looks good, I will share a draft SLA_Annex_draft.docx and a one-page amendment to the master agreement.
3) If procurement wants to move fast, we can pre-populate a DocuSign for signatures once terms are agreed.

Would end of next week for a formal estimate work for you?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: Linestream_MA_plan_v3.pdf (outline of proposed term changes)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Linestream renewal — need pricing + ops confirmation (do not externalize)

Karthik / Priyom — forwarding a request from Anya at Linestream. They want Premium SLA + p95 <=300ms + +4 GPUs reserved (+burst). They are current Dedicated customer with a modest committed base. Key items for you to validate:

- Pricing: please run committed + reserved GPU uplift and a couple of consumption scenarios (baseline, +25% seasonal, +60% holiday spike) and show monthly burn and effective per-token delta. I need a firm uplift number and what discounts (if any) apply for 12/24 month term.
- Technical ops: can we guarantee p95 300ms for their main chat route in us-west with a +4 GPU reservation? If p99 degrades, propose mitigations (fallback model variant, burst routing, autoscale windows).
- Support: confirm SLA wording for 30-minute Sev1 response and outline oncall rotation and escalation names. Also suggest a runbook template we can share.

I attached the MA plan I sent them. Can you get an initial read by COB Mon 20th? I will then share the SLA_Annex_draft.docx with them.

Thanks — Vanessa

Attachment: Linestream_MA_plan_v3.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Linestream renewal — need pricing + ops confirmation (do not externalize)

Vanessa, Priyom — initial read below. Short version: feasible, with the following guardrails and tradeoffs.

Pricing (high level):
- Committed uplift for +4 GPUs (12-month term) -> estimated +19% on current committed spend. +22% for 24-month term due to capacity reservation profile. I will attach a scenario sheet to the HubSpot deal.
- Burst pool charged as overage at a reduced blended rate; recommend we offer 6 months of capped burst credits to ease adoption.

Technical:
- p95 <= 300ms is achievable for the primary chat route if we:
  - Pin the route to dedicated pool in us-west and enable KV prefix caching and optimized batching.
  - Reserve CPU & network egress QoS on the nodes for the account.
- p99 tail risk: during correlated spikes p99 can hit ~700ms without mitigation. Mitigations: lightweight fallback model (quantized variant), short TTL caching, and a pre-warm window during expected spikes.

Support / Runbook:
- We can commit to 30-min Sev1 initial response and named oncall. Priyom to confirm who the named oncall is and roster. Priyom: can you share the draft runbook?

Action items: Karthik to upload pricing scenarios to HubSpot by Mon 20th; Priyom to draft runbook and confirm oncall names.

— Karthik

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Linestream renewal — need pricing + ops confirmation (do not externalize)

Quick updates:
- Runbook: attached draft runbook (we'll share clean copy externally). It includes escalation matrix, playbook for degraded latency, and warmup steps for burst windows.
- Oncall: named primary oncall for Linestream will be Maya (platform ops), secondary is Julian (infra). We'll provide a calendar with rotation weeks.
- Capacity: reservation +4 GPUs looks fine; recommend autoscale cooldown of 5 minutes and a warmup pre-scale window of 15 minutes for predictable traffic.

I will link the runbook into the HubSpot deal and send the cleaned SLA_Annex_draft.docx once pricing is locked.

— Priyom

Attachment: SLA_Annex_draft.docx

From: Anya Patel <anya@linestream.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@linestream.com>, Linestream Procurement <procure@linestream.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: SLA + capacity questions for upcoming term

Vanessa — thank you, that all sounds reasonable. A couple of follow-ups from procurement / legal:

- Can you provide the exact credit calculation language for the 99.9% uptime SLA? Procurement needs to map it to our internal approval flow.
- We'd like to cap the financial exposure for both sides in the first term; open to a not-to-exceed credit cap or a stepped credit schedule.
- For the latency SLO, can you include a clause that allows a temporary model-fallback solution for 3rd-party tooling if p99 thresholds are triggered? We understand mitigation is necessary but want transparency when fallback is used.

If you can get us a redline-ready SLA annex and a pricing worksheet I can share with finance, procurement will aim to respond within 48 hours.

Best,
Anya

Anya / Carlos — following up with the deliverables you asked for. See links and attachments:

- SLA_Annex_draft.docx (attached) — includes uptime credit formula with a tiered cap: first breach triggers service credits up to 5% of monthly committed spend, subsequent sustained breaches escalate to a 15% cap for the month. We noted procurement's request about not-to-exceed language and added a mutual cap clause for the first 12 months.
- Pricing worksheet (uploaded to HubSpot) — includes baseline, +25% and +60% scenarios, and a recommended 12-month term price (+19% uplift).
- Runbook (attached) — named oncall roster and escalation matrix.

We're also happy to carve out a short call with Legal/Procurement to walk the credit language and make quick redlines — I'm free Thu 23rd 9am or Fri 24th 2pm PT. Please tell me which works and I'll calendar.

If that aligns, we'll prepare a DocuSign set with the MA amendment and SLA annex so you can route to finance and legal.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this and setting up the QBR cadence.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
